title: Chapter jump rail: a scrollspy of real links that jumps, lands on the heading and lets go
intent: Chapter jump rail and scrollspy index
summary: One fixed `<nav aria-label>` of six numbered chapter links whose current one (`aria-current="true"`) is the chapter with its midpoint nearest the viewport centre (none above the first chapter or below the last), measured from cached offsets once per Lenis scroll event; a 2 px rule under each name fills with `scaleX` from the reading position (done chapters full, the current one at the centre line's share of its height); one 3 px marker centred on the list's 1 px track moves by a written `translate3d` on the routine band (`.4 s` expo-out) and cuts when it first appears; any in-page chapter link jumps with `lenis.scrollTo` (`1.2 s`, Lenis on the GSAP ticker, `scroll-margin-top` honoured, the glide named by `userData`), marks the destination at the start and holds it until landing, then focuses the chapter heading (`tabindex=-1`, `preventScroll`, the only announcement; no live region) and replaces the hash; a `touchmove`, wheel or scrolling key mid-glide stops the glide where it is (`lenis.stop(); lenis.start()`) with no landing, a tap does not, and a check every `1.8 s` waits for a late glide and lets go of a replaced one; below 900 px the same list sits behind a sticky ticket ("Stage n of 6" + short title, described as opening the list) with its own progress rule, docked by a `0.5 s` glide when opened off the top, a disclosure (`aria-expanded`) closed by Escape, outside taps, Tab out and a jump, which parks focus on the ticket for the glide; reduced and static tiers (by media query or `html[data-motion]`) jump and dock instantly, cut the marker and chevron and keep the current link, fills and focus move; the six height profiles share one 0–600 m scale; forced colours outline the current link
variants: a fixed rail beside the read, a sticky ticket on phones (this, default)
the rail rotated with `writing-mode: vertical-rl` against the right edge, for a page that cannot spare a column
chapters of very unequal length: mark the chapter containing the centre line instead of the nearest midpoint
on a virtual scroll: map the same list to section indices and jump by seeking the scalar
